config.title: will-change

intro.title: will-change
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with a button that smoothly changes color when hovered over, using the CSS `will-change` property to optimize performance. You will learn how `will-change` hints to the browser about elements that are likely to change, allowing it to prepare resources in advance for smoother animations. The main technologies involved are CSS for styling and the `will-change` property specifically for performance optimization. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you understand when and how to apply `will-change` to improve user experience without overusing it.
intro.usecase: The `will-change` property is used by developers to optimize performance in complex, interactive user interfaces. For example, in a data dashboard with real-time updating charts or a scrolling news feed with parallax effects, applying `will-change` to the animated elements can prevent jank by hinting to the browser which properties are likely to change. This is crucial for maintaining smooth animations in product carousels, expanding side panels, or draggable modal windows, ensuring a polished user experience. By strategically using `will-change`, developers can proactively manage rendering performance in dynamic web applications.

objectives: Apply the will-change property to optimize CSS animations
Configure will-change values for specific transform properties
Initialize will-change states for hover interactions
Manipulate will-change declarations to improve scrolling performance
Integrate will-change with existing CSS transition rules
Control browser rendering hints using targeted will-change values
Update element styles to include will-change for opacity animations

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure with elements to animate
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML file with a container div and several child div elements that will serve as animation targets.
steps.hint: Start with a basic HTML structure that includes a container element and multiple child elements inside it.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>CSS will-change Demo</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add your container and child elements here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: A basic HTML file with a container div and several child div elements that can be animated with CSS.
successCriteria: HTML file contains a container div with multiple child div elements inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You have some HTML structure, but make sure you have a container div with multiple child div elements inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure doesn't match what's needed. Create a container div with several child div elements.

steps.title: Add basic CSS styling and positioning for the elements
steps.instruction: Open your styles.css file and add CSS rules to style the body with a background color and center its content.
steps.hint: Use the body selector and set properties like background-color and text-align.
steps.expectedOutcome: The body will have a light gray background and centered content.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a body selector with at least background-color and text-align properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include both background-color and text-align properties for the body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS doesn't yet style the body as requested. Add a body selector with background-color and text-align properties.

steps.title: Create a CSS animation using @keyframes
steps.instruction: Define a @keyframes animation named 'moveAndTransform' that moves an element horizontally and rotates it.
steps.hint: Use @keyframes with the animation name, then define keyframes like 0% and 100% with transform properties.

steps.expectedOutcome: A @keyframes animation named 'moveAndTransform' is defined with transform properties for movement and rotation.
successCriteria: The @keyframes rule is present with the name 'moveAndTransform', and includes at least one transform property (e.g., translate, rotate) within the keyframes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the animation is named 'moveAndTransform' and includes transform properties like translate or rotate.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation definition is missing or incorrect. Check that you used @keyframes with the correct name and included transform properties.

steps.title: Apply the animation to elements without will-change
steps.instruction: Add the animation property to your elements to apply the keyframes animation you created earlier.
steps.hint: Use the animation property with the animation name and duration, for example: animation: slide 2s infinite;
steps.expectedOutcome: The elements will start animating with the default browser rendering behavior.
successCriteria: The animation property is applied to at least one element with the correct animation name and duration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some animation properties, but make sure to include both the animation name and duration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation isn't applied correctly. Check that you're using the animation property with the correct animation name from your @keyframes.

steps.title: Introduce the will-change property syntax
steps.instruction: Add the will-change property to the element's CSS rule, setting it to 'transform'.
steps.hint: Use the CSS property 'will-change' with the value 'transform' inside the element's selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The element's CSS rule now includes will-change: transform;
successCriteria: The CSS contains 'will-change: transform;' within the element's selector.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added 'will-change: transform;' to the element's CSS rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The will-change property with value 'transform' is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add will-change: transform to animated elements
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property will-change: transform; to the elements that will be animated with transform properties.
steps.hint: Place the will-change property inside the CSS rule for the elements you are animating.
steps.expectedOutcome: The will-change property is added to the CSS rules for the animated elements, hinting to the browser that transform animations will occur.
successCriteria: The CSS includes will-change: transform; applied to the elements that will be animated with transform properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added will-change, but make sure it's specifically set to 'transform' and applied to the correct elements that will be animated.
steps.feedbackWrong: The will-change property is not correctly added. Ensure you add 'will-change: transform;' to the CSS rules for the elements that will be animated with transform properties.

steps.title: Compare animation performance with and without will-change
steps.instruction: Add a comment in your CSS to note where you'll test the animation with will-change enabled versus disabled.
steps.hint: You can add a comment like /* Test with will-change enabled */ or /* Compare performance here */ near your will-change property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A comment is added to your CSS file to indicate where you'll compare animation performance.
successCriteria: A CSS comment exists in the code that mentions testing or comparing performance with will-change.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a comment, but make sure it clearly indicates where you'll test animation performance with will-change.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a CSS comment that mentions testing or comparing performance with will-change.

steps.title: Add will-change: opacity for fade animations
steps.instruction: Create a new @keyframes rule named 'fadeInOut' that animates opacity from 0 to 1 and back to 0.
steps.hint: Define a @keyframes rule with the name 'fadeInOut' and specify opacity values at 0%, 50%, and 100% keyframes.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new @keyframes rule named 'fadeInOut' is created with opacity animation keyframes.
successCriteria: The @keyframes rule is named 'fadeInOut' and includes opacity values at 0%, 50%, and 100%.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your @keyframes rule is named 'fadeInOut' and includes opacity values at 0%, 50%, and 100%.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @keyframes rule should be named 'fadeInOut' with opacity animation. Try defining it with three keyframes: 0% opacity 0, 50% opacity 1, and 100% opacity 0.

steps.title: Understand when NOT to use will-change
steps.instruction: Add a CSS comment explaining that will-change should be used sparingly and only on elements that will actually change.
steps.hint: Write a CSS comment using /* */ syntax. Mention that overusing will-change can cause performance issues.
steps.analogousExample: /* Good practice: only use will-change on elements you're about to animate */
steps.expectedOutcome: The learner adds a CSS comment explaining best practices for will-change usage.
successCriteria: A CSS comment is added that mentions will-change should be used sparingly and only on elements that will actually change.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a comment, but it doesn't fully explain when not to use will-change. Make sure your comment mentions that will-change should be used sparingly and only on elements that will actually change.
steps.feedbackWrong: No comment was added. Add a CSS comment explaining that will-change should be used sparingly and only on elements that will actually change.

steps.title: Create a practical example with hover effects using will-change
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a button that changes background color and scale on hover, using will-change to optimize the transform property.
steps.hint: Define a button selector with a transition for transform and background-color, then use :hover to change those properties. Add will-change: transform; to the button's base style.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button that smoothly scales and changes color on hover, with will-change applied to the transform property to optimize performance.
successCriteria: Button selector defined with base styles
will-change: transform; present in base style
:hover state changes background-color and transform: scale()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your button has will-change: transform; in its base style, and the hover state changes both background-color and transform with a scale value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a button with a hover effect that changes background-color and scale, and add will-change: transform; to optimize the animation.
